title: FEANEL: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Error Analysis in K-12 English Writing
extended_summary:
This paper introduces FEANEL, a benchmark for fine-grained error analysis in K-12 English writing. The authors argue that while large language models have shown promise for educational applications, their ability to provide detailed, pedagogically useful feedback on student writing remains underexplored. FEANEL is designed to evaluate whether LLMs can classify individual writing errors, rate their severity, and generate explanations that are accurate and instructional rather than merely corrective.

The benchmark contains 1,000 anonymized essays written by K-12 learners, split evenly between elementary-school students and secondary-school students, and annotated by English education experts. The data were collected from a global online education platform and the TECCL corpus, then cleaned to remove off-topic, nonsensical, incomplete, or error-free essays. Experts developed a 29-category error taxonomy and produced gold-standard labels for error type, severity, and explanatory feedback. The paper evaluates multiple state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-4o, o1, o3, Gemini-2.5-pro, Claude-3.7, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-3, and Llama-3 variants, under zero-shot and one-shot prompting conditions.

The main finding is that current LLMs remain substantially below human teachers on this fine-grained writing-analysis task, especially for classification of complex errors and for generating high-quality explanations. Performance improves with richer prompts and examples, and larger or reasoning-oriented models often do better, but no model dominates across all sub-tasks. The paper concludes that fine-grained educational feedback for K-12 writing is still a difficult problem and that better task-specific model alignment, prompting, and evaluation methods are needed.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic large language model/chatbot systems used to analyze writing errors and generate pedagogically oriented explanations or feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper benchmarks multiple state-of-the-art LLMs on a K-12 English writing benchmark (FEANEL) for fine-grained error classification, severity rating, and explanation generation.

findings.finding_summary: On the FEANEL benchmark, current LLMs showed substantial limitations in fine-grained writing error analysis for K-12 English essays. Human teachers outperformed all evaluated models on error classification and explanation, and the paper reports that LLM explanations had low BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE compared with other generation tasks, indicating weak pedagogical feedback quality. No effect sizes or CIs were reported.
findings.measure: Error classification accuracy/Macro-F1, severity MAE, and explanation quality (BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE-L) on 1,000 essays

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark and model-evaluation paper, not a randomized or quasi-experimental study of instructional impact in classrooms. The evidence is methodological/benchmarking in nature rather than causal evidence about reading or literacy outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports clear model-performance differences on error-analysis metrics, but no educational effect size is provided and the results do not establish impact on student literacy outcomes. The strongest evidence is descriptive: LLMs perform below human teachers, especially on explanation quality and complex error classification.
